(1) Token: DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION

(2) Expansion statement: Fix the graphtor-docs MCP entry's dependency/generation-safety gaps in .mcp.json -- (a) the shim executable .copilot/graphtor-mcp-shim.cjs is gitignored/untracked and not verified by any install/tune flow, so a fresh clone can launch Copilot but cannot start the graphtor-docs MCP server until that shim is separately generated; (b) the entry's x-graphtor-managed: true marker opts it into generate_mcp_config's managed-entry contract (src/workspace/mcp_config.rs:197-212,526-543), which rewrites every marked entry to its canonical {command, args:["serve"], transport} shape on the next graphtor-docs install, silently discarding this entry's custom bun-shim command/args/type/tools fields.

(3) Out-of-scope rationale (P-021 C1): both sub-issues require either a Rust source change to the graphtor-docs install/tune MCP-config generation logic (src/workspace/mcp_config.rs) or a broader design decision about how a custom MCP entry should be verified/preserved across installs (a distinct autoharness marker, or teaching the generator to preserve a managed-but-custom shape) -- decisions well beyond "completing the exact change already authorized" for this branch's startup/checkpoint-recovery fix. This is an architecture decision for the graphtor-docs MCP generation system itself, not a startup-script fix, and requires Stage triage/deliberation.

(4) Source refs: task ID N/A (no active shipment/task this session), feature ID N/A, shipment ID N/A (chore-branch-only session; no shipment claimed or mutated per operator instruction), branch fix/graphtor-startup-checkpoint-recovery @ 25a1290652ebc0eb42885e035d2ac7a76d1ba73e, PR number 118, review-thread ID PRRT_kwDORiB5E86fdtzs (Copilot-authored thread on .mcp.json:20/21, PR #118).

DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION

(1) Token: DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION

(2) Expansion statement: Add real Windows-ACL owner-only enforcement (a Windows-specific security-descriptor/ACL check restricting access to the current OS user) to the probe workspace created by tools/mcp-probe/src/workspace.rs, so a different local user on the same Windows machine cannot read or tamper with the isolated probe workspace's control/treatment .mcp.json fixtures -- a gap identified by Copilot review on PR #120 (thread at workspace.rs:460).

(3) Out-of-scope rationale (P-021 C1): 056.021-T's own acceptance criteria explicitly state the accepted threat model: "the probe-local, std-only canonicalize/symlink_metadata check protects against accidental escape ... It does not defend against a malicious same-user process that can modify source or the workspace, and the std-only check's TOCTOU window is an accepted residual risk for this non-sensitive, same-user diagnostic workspace." Copilot's finding describes a DIFFERENT, broader threat (a different LOCAL USER via OS-level ACL/permissions, not the already-accepted same-user TOCTOU risk), which 056.021-T never scoped in. The same task's own acceptance criteria also explicitly state: "Own ONLY tools/mcp-probe/src/workspace.rs ... MUST NOT import graphtor_core and MUST NOT duplicate or claim a reusable production security primitive; use only a probe-local, std-only containment check." Implementing genuine Windows ACL/security-descriptor enforcement requires either a new platform-specific Windows API dependency (e.g. windows-acl/winapi security-descriptor bindings) or duplicating/importing a security primitive -- both explicitly forbidden by this task's own "std-only" constraint. Copilot's alternative suggestion (fail closed on Windows when ACL enforcement is unavailable) would additionally break the tool entirely on the Windows platform this same regression (049-S) targets, a functional regression far beyond a bug fix. This is new design/implementation scope, not completion of any already-authorized change, so it fails the same-contract-surface test.

(4) Source refs: task ID 056.021-T (owns tools/mcp-probe/src/workspace.rs and its containment threat model); feature ID 056-F (covering feature, intentionally excluded from 049-S's manifest per operator scope); shipment ID 049-S; PR number 120; review-thread ID PRRT_kwDORiB5E86h1QZL (Copilot-authored thread on workspace.rs:460).

(5) Requires deliberation: true (needs a Constitution Check for the new Windows-ACL/security-descriptor design -- dependency selection, cross-platform fallback behavior, blast-radius/perf tradeoffs -- before this can be planned as a task).

(6) Kind: chore; provisional priority: medium (defense-in-depth hardening against a same-machine different-local-user actor on a non-sensitive, transient, diagnostic-only probe workspace; no known active exploitation path and the task's own reviewed acceptance criteria explicitly accepted a narrower same-user TOCTOU risk already; re-prioritization remains Stage-only).

DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION

(1) Token: DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION

(2) Expansion statement: `main.rs`'s `run_wrapper_subcommand` (the standalone `mcp-probe wrapper` CLI entry point) collapses the full `WrapperOutcome` returned by `process::run_wrapper` down to a bare process exit code (`outcome.inner_exit_code.unwrap_or(1)`), discarding `residual_descendants`, `wrapper_identity`/`sentinel_inherited`, and any `evidence_write_error` entirely for a caller invoking this subcommand directly (not through `056.001-T`'s `exact-cli` classification pipeline). Copilot review (PR #120, round 5) flagged this data loss. Round 5's `inner_teardown_incomplete` completion (this same PR) addresses the safety-critical gating half of this finding via a new `EvidenceCollector::note_inner_teardown_incomplete` call in `run_wrapper` that marks the persisted `--evidence-output` JSON `valid: false` when teardown could not be confirmed -- which `leg_has_valid_initialize` (`exact_cli.rs`) already reads and gates on for the production `exact-cli` classification pipeline. What remains unaddressed is presentation-only: a caller who runs the bare `mcp-probe wrapper` subcommand directly still gets no visibility into `residual_descendants`, `wrapper_identity`/`sentinel_inherited`, `inner_teardown_incomplete`, or `evidence_write_error` beyond the exit code, since this subcommand intentionally persists no evidence of its own ("serializing to --evidence-output is 056.023-T's job" per its own doc comment).

(3) Out-of-scope rationale (P-021 C1): fixing this requires a genuinely new design decision -- what output format/channel to add (stderr diagnostic lines? a `--json` flag printing the full `WrapperOutcome`? always-on structured stdout, which could be a breaking change for any existing caller parsing today's bare exit code?) -- for a standalone CLI subcommand whose current documented contract is deliberately minimal ("persists no evidence itself"). None of 049-S's 8 manifest tasks scoped adding a new output surface or CLI flag to this subcommand; the same-contract-surface completion available this round (the evidence-file gating fix) has already been applied and is the part with actual safety impact (production classification correctness). Adding a new CLI output surface is new scope, not a completion of the already-authorized change.

(4) Source refs: task ID 056.001-T (owns main.rs's wrapper/exact-cli subcommand wiring) plus 056.022-T/056.023-T (process/evidence contract this finding touches), feature ID 056-F (covering feature, intentionally excluded from 049-S's manifest per Stage handoff), shipment ID 049-S, branch chore/fix-mcp-serve-initialize-handshake-regression, PR number 120, review-thread ID PRRT_kwDORiB5E86h2RnM (Copilot-authored thread on main.rs:102).

(5) Requires deliberation: true (needs a design decision on the new output surface/format and whether it is a breaking change to the subcommand's current minimal contract, before this can be planned as a task).

(6) Kind: task; provisional priority: low (the safety-critical half -- evidence-file gating for the production exact-cli classification path -- is already fixed this round; this residual is presentation/observability-only for a standalone direct-invocation path with no known production caller today).
